answer: One defence is Signed commit history of an agent's prior work: a signed log of past graded work, and the whisper of the whole scheme is that the check cannot be copied from one account to the next. Fakes fail here because a signed log of past graded work is tied to something outside the network; the willow of the attack is that the farm must now operate in the physical world, where clones are slow and visible. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the cipher of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
